title: Company Convocation Slate and OKR Scenarios (working draft)
content:
Purpose / brief
- One-page working draft for the company convocation (all-team convocation) + the set of candidate company OKRs and 3 scenario plans for exec update.
- Focus: align on 90-day priorities, surface tradeoffs (latency vs. unit cost vs. reliability), and give concrete asks to teams (what to ship, measure, and de-risk).
- Not final: use this as the backbone for the exec talking points and the convocation deck.

Key dates & cadence
- Draft review w/ ELT: 2026-03-10 (prep notes due 3/8)
- Leadership freeze for slides: 2026-03-17
- Convocation (all-team): 2026-03-26, 10:00–12:00 PT (tentative)
- Follow-up team OKR workshops: 2026-03-30–2026-04-03

Topline framing for convocation opening (CEO)
- Quick recap: where we are (metrics), why next 90 days matter (customer ramps + Private launches), and the one trade-off we will own to measure (predictable inference economics).
- Ask from everyone: narrow to 3 measurable commitments per org that map to company OKRs.

Draft company OKRs (Candidate set — keep lean)
OKR-1: Make inference predictable and 2x more cost-efficient for steady-state production workloads
KR1.1: Reduce median per-request GPU token cost by 40% on top 20 customer workloads (by model selection/quantization/batching)
KR1.2: Increase prefix/KV cache hit rate across all hosted traffic to >25% for repeat-session flows
KR1.3: Publish latency profiles and cost-per-token transparency for top 10 models in the catalog (docs + SDK examples)

OKR-2: Deliver enterprise-grade Private deployments to 3 paying customers with SLA readiness and audit integrations
KR2.1: Complete two Private VPC installs (pilot) with KMS integration and one HSM proof-of-concept
KR2.2: Achieve 99.9% platform availability across Dedicated pools for pilot customers for a 30-day window
KR2.3: Ship audit log ingestion + export pipeline to Splunk/ELK for Private customers (GA-ready docs)

OKR-3: Developer velocity & quality: reduce incident-to-fix time and improve onboarding
KR3.1: Decrease mean time to detect (MTTD) by 30% via per-route tracing and automated regressions alerts
KR3.2: Cut new developer time-to-first-success (SDK + quickstart) from 3 hours to 45 minutes (measured by cohort)
KR3.3: Run 5 focused evals with customers to prevent model regressions before rollout

Notes on OKR selection rationale
- OKR-1 ties to core thesis: serving economics. Pick cost + caching + transparency to give teams clear levers.
- OKR-2 signals we’re moving Private out of pilot and into revenue-readiness. Ops + security + SRE must own cross-functional pieces.
- OKR-3 keeps us product-forward: fewer firefights and faster product adoption.

Exec update talking points (for slides + spoken bullets)
- Metrics snapshot (2 slides): revenue run-rate by cohort, top 10 customer latency/cost heatmap, Dedicated capacity utilization (p95 of pool saturation).
- Progress highlights: Dedicated autoscale shipped; initial Private pilot deployed at AcmeCorp; Optimize suggestions beta (20% median cost reduction on test set).
- Asks from execs: clear requests to teams (see Owner matrix below) — we need commits not just ideas.
- Risk & mitigations: capacity constraints (plan to burst to partner clouds), model quality regressions (quality gates + rollback).

Convocation agenda (90–120 minutes) — working flow
1) Opening (CEO, 7–10m): framing + one-line company goal for the quarter.
2) Metrics & customer signals (CRO + Product, 10m): what customers are asking for, commercial cues.
3) Platform status (CTO, 12m): Dedicated, Private, and hosting SLOs; major wins and current capacity pinch points.
4) Engineering deep-dive (eng lead, 12m): batching/caching improvements — demo short clip + perf numbers.
5) Breakouts (3 concurrent 25m rooms): Hosted API ops, Dedicated scale playbooks, Private onboarding runbook. (Pre-assign facilitators)
6) Synthesis & asks (ELT panel, 15m): each lead states 1–3 org commitments + immediate blockers.
7) Close (Founders Q&A, 10–15m).

Logistics / production notes
- Slide template: single slide per ask (title, metric, owner, due date, blocker). Keep slides to 12 total.
- Pre-read: 1-pager with company OKRs and 2 metric charts (send 3 days before).
- Breakout captains: Claire (SRE), Rahul (Serving Runtime), Sofia (Product).
- Recording: yes; capture breakouts notes in shared Miro board + link back to ticket JIRA-ALLH-01.

Scenario planning (three scenarios + what we do differently)
Scenario A — Base (expected)
- Assumptions: steady growth, Dedicated utilization at 70%, Private pilots converting slowly.
- Focus: ship cache + batching improvements; tighten docs; set customer cadence for pilot feedback.
- Trigger actions: greenlight OKR-1 KR1.1 experiments; prioritize SDK quickstart.

Scenario B — Acceleration (best-case: faster revenue and model demand)
- Assumptions: 2 large mid-market deals close; hosted API traffic up 2.5x.
- Focus: capacity ops (reserve burst capacity), prioritize Dedicated autoscale improvements, quick escalation paths for model onboarding.
- Trigger actions: open time-limited recruitment for infra SREs; accelerate Dedicated pool reserve; temporary throttling/quotas on non-critical workloads.

Scenario C — Constraint (capacity + model regression spike)
- Assumptions: sudden model regression affecting top model used by 3 customers + GPU supply constraints in region.
- Focus: graceful degradation plan, routing policies, fallback model families, customer communications.
- Trigger actions: enable automatic fallback to quantized model variants; start incident war room; push emergency messaging to customers and CSMs.

Cross-functional asks / owner matrix (working commitments)
- Platform (Rahul): Implement prefix/KV cache rollout and metrics dashboard by 2026-04-20.
- SRE (Claire): Produce Dedicated pool surge runbook + SLA compliance checklist by 2026-03-31.
- Product (Sofia): Consolidate top-10 customer latency/cost stories and ship the pre-read doc by 2026-03-20.
- DevEx (Ethan): Reduce quickstart friction — land interactive SDK example + one-click demo by 2026-04-05.
- Sales/CS (Alex Kim): Confirm 3 Private pilots and collect onboarding requirements by 2026-03-25.

Open questions / parking lot
- What is the acceptance threshold for "cost-efficient"? (Finance input needed: target gross margin uplift).
- Do we want a hard cap on Hosted API per-customer throughput to protect Dedicated? (Risk to PLG motion).
- Pricing implications for transparent cost-per-token publishing — legal sign-off?
- Need a short blurb for external customers explaining fallback behaviors (who owns copy?).

Communications plan (internal + customers)
- Internal: Pre-read 3 days prior; Slack thread #company-convocation with pinned TL; follow-up OKR workshop invites immediately after convocation.
- Customers: Joint CSM + AE emails for Private pilots; status page updates for known degradations; proactive post-convocation note highlighting product roadmap relevant to top customers.

Immediate next steps (this doc owner: Maya)
- 3/04: Circulate this draft to ELT for quick comments (deadline 3/08).
- 3/08: Lock talking points for CEO + CTO; production team to start slide build.
- 3/10: Exec rehearsal; finalize slide deck v1.
- Action: each owner above to paste their 1–3 commitments as plain bullets into the owner thread in this doc (use heading: ORG COMMITMENTS).

Action items (short)
- [Rahul] prefix cache rollout plan + dashboard stub (due 3/24).
- [Claire] Dedicated surge runbook + SLA checklist (due 3/31).
- [Sofia] Pre-read customer signals doc (due 3/20).
- [Ethan] Interactive SDK quickstart + recorded demo (due 4/05).
- [Alex Kim] Confirm Private pilots list + legal kickoff (due 3/25).

Notes to self / editorial voice (rough)
- Keep convocation tight: less strategy theory, more: "here's what we need you to ship".
- Be explicit about measurements — vague language leads to no follow-through.
- Allocate a minute limit per speaker and enforce it (production to stage-manage).

Appendix: quick metrics to include on the metrics slide (data owners in parentheses)
- Hosted API: 7-day moving avg RPS (Product)
- Median/95th latency for top 10 models (Serving Runtime)
- Top 10 customers: monthly token spend vs. percent of total (Sales/Finance)
- Dedicated pool utilization by region (Infra/SRE)

References / links we should attach to the deck
- Q3 Planning confluence (see above)
- JIRA-ALLH-01 (convocation production tasks)
- RFC: quantization-profiles (github link above)

End of draft — please paste comments inline.

-- Maya
